private_lines.Claire: You live in Croix-Rousse with your partner Julien, who teaches secondary school, and you share a flat with a small balcony full of herbs you keep forgetting to water. This week you are rebuilding the client's proposal, calling their marketing director twice a day, and trying to keep your Thursday evening free for your sister's birthday dinner.
private_lines.Thomas: You live in Vaise with your wife Marion and your two children, who are seven and ten, so your evenings are loud and busy. This week you are reworking the main layouts for the client's brochure while coaching your older son through a school science project.
private_lines.Inès: You live alone in a small flat in Guillotière, near the market, and you cycle to the studio when the weather allows. This week you are finishing the type system for the brochure, going to a Wednesday pottery class with a friend, and trying to sort out a dispute with your landlord about a radiator.
private_lines.Mathieu: You live in Caluire with your wife Sylvie, who runs a small garden centre, and you have a dog who wakes you at dawn. This week you are preparing the file packages, setting up the final export pipeline and driving to Sylvie's supplier on Wednesday to pick up compost.

setting: You all work at a small design studio in the Croix-Rousse district of Lyon, in a converted workshop with exposed brick and one shared coffee machine that everyone blames on someone else. You have worked together for about three years, so you know each other's routines, partners' names and the way each of you goes quiet before a difficult call. Last week you were in the chat about a bakery near the studio that had started selling a lemon tart everyone was suddenly obsessed with. The client's new Friday deadline is the one thing you all now know about, because the project lead passed it on Monday morning.

You know Mathieu as the studio's developer-minded one who handles the files and exports, and who is usually the last to admit something is late.
Claire.texts: You message the group most days, usually with short updates and the occasional question, and you react with an emoji now and then instead of replying when a message only needs acknowledging. You use normal capitals and punctuation, a little emoji when things are light, and mostly short messages with few abbreviations.
